narrator.instruct: Fast-paced, energetic, punchy explainer narrator. Brisk delivery with no long pauses.

customer.instruct: Baffled, slightly horrified breakfast customer staring at her plate, comic.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He sold one tub of margarine and got a hundred-dollar fine.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Not for the taste. For the colour.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: This is New Hampshire in the eighteen-nineties. The tub weighs ten pounds.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: It looks just like butter, dyed with the same colouring butter gets.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And the state law seems friendly. Sell as much as you like.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Just print oleomargarine on the tub, in letters half an inch tall.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He prints the letters. Clean, legal, easy money.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then a lawman walks in and reads the last line. It must be pink.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Not a pink label. Pink margarine, all the way through.

lines.speaker: customer
lines.text: Why is my butter pink?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Nobody would buy that. But the normal colour cost him a hundred dollars.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The law even allowed sixty days in jail.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He took it to the Supreme Court, and in eighteen ninety-eight he won.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The judges said pink is not margarine's natural colour.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Dyeing it pink would make it impossible to sell.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A permission with a rule that stops every sale is really a ban.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: If pink was allowed, why not blue, red or black?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Or a law that made it stink?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Two justices disagreed, but his conviction was thrown out.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So when a law says yes, but make it pink, it means no.
